audit.whatIsWrong: Singed wins 45.87% over 835 games — his worst lane in this slice — yet both layers score him four of the seven stages: Urgot, Skill, Singed, Singed, Urgot, Singed, Singed.
audit.why: A chart that hands the majority of the lane to the champion losing it by more than eight points contradicts the headline number printed directly above it. The packet chart reads Urgot, Skill, Skill, Singed, Urgot, Singed, Urgot, which is honest: Singed keeps the two stages he genuinely owns (the 4-5 proxy window and the Rylai's spike) and gives back level 3 and the two-item stage. Level 3 is not Singed's — whys[2] already says 'the lane stays contested' and 'his W still wins the straight duel', so the cell disagrees with its own why. The two-item stage is Urgot's: Purge costs nothing and has no cooldown at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Chart moved as one group to the packet read across both layers; the two flipped stages' why lines rewritten to state the reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike list picks the right four moments but attaches no numbers to any of them, and the two-item stage is never identified as a spike for Urgot at all.
audit.why: Purge is the spike nobody wrote down. Its cooldown is 12/9/6/3/0 and its cost is 40/30/20/10/0 — at rank 5 it is free and permanently available, which is a different ability from the 12-second, 40-mana version Singed faces at level 3. That is exactly why the two-item stage belongs to Urgot. Fear Beyond Death is 100/85/70, so his execute window tightens by thirty seconds across the game while Insanity Potion stays flat at 100.
audit.corrected: Purge's 12/9/6/3/0 progression and Fear Beyond Death's 100/85/70 written into breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2].why, phases[6].why and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: Disdain shields Urgot. Riot's text: 'Urgot charges in a direction, shielding himself and trampling non-champion enemies. If he catches an enemy champion, he will stop and hurl them out of his way.' Neither layer mentions the shield, and neither mentions that it tramples minions.
audit.why: Both halves change how a Singed plays the lane and both are absent. The shield means Urgot's engage is also his defensive cooldown — committing into a fresh Disdain means fighting through absorbed damage on top of the flip, so it has to be baited out first, and the _missing file flags exactly this rule for the pair. The trampling half kills the page's implicit assumption that a thick wave protects you: it does not, because Disdain runs straight through minions and only stops on a champion. A proxying Singed sitting behind his own wave is not screened at all.
audit.corrected: Disdain (E): 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s, 475 range. It shields him on the charge and tramples minions, stopping only on a champion — the wave does not screen it. Bait it, then commit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (Disdain description, shield flag, cooldown 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, range 475)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text, early and whys[0] all state that Corrosive Charge deals percent-max-HP damage. Riot's description of Corrosive Charge is 'Fires an explosive charge at the target location, dealing physical damage and slowing enemies caught in the explosion.'
audit.why: Nothing about the ability is percent-health, and the page uses the claim to tell a Singed that his tankiness 'means nothing right now' — which is build advice derived from a false premise. Physical damage plus a slow from 800 range on a 10/9.5/9/8.5/8 cooldown is the real threat, and it is a threat armour genuinely answers. The slow is also the setup half of the kill combo the page describes further down, so naming it correctly makes the level-2 warning actionable.
audit.corrected: Corrosive Charge (Q): physical damage and a slow, 800 range, 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s. It is the lock-on for the Disdain flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: Purge slows Urgot himself. Riot's text: 'Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies.' The page treats Purge purely as a threat and never mentions the self-slow. Fear Beyond Death's 2500 range is also absent.
audit.why: The self-slow is the Singed player's exit. Purge is 490 range and Urgot is slower while firing it, so the moment he commits to W is the moment his chase is at its weakest — that is when you walk out through your own trail, not before. And 2500 range on Fear Beyond Death means he can impale a proxying Singed from most of the way across the lane; 'never commit an all-in at half HP' understates it, because you do not have to be near him at all.
audit.corrected: Purge: 490 range, and it slows Urgot while he fires — that is your window to leave. Fear Beyond Death: 2500 range, 100/85/70s, so distance is not safety.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (Purge description and range 490, Fear Beyond Death range 2500 and cooldown 100/85/70)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Disdain with no number and fills the remaining two lines with generic placeholder text.
audit.why: Disdain at 16/15.5/15/14.5/14 barely scales, so the punish window stays roughly constant all game and is the one reliable cooldown to play around. Purge going to zero at rank 5 means there is no window on it at all late — advice that says 'wait for his cooldown' is wrong after that point and the page needs to say so.

The kit file marks Corrosive Charge with a 'dash' flag. Riot's own description is 'Fires an explosive charge at the target location' — a thrown charge, not movement. This is a tooltip-parsing misfire and I wrote nothing based on it. Disdain is the ability that actually moves Urgot.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (Corrosive Charge description vs dash flag)

edits.before: Urgot owns levels 1-2 hard — his Corrosive Charge (Q) poke reaches you before you are near him, and his Purge (W) shotgun legs deal percent-max-HP so your future tankiness means nothing right now. Do not try to trade; set up your proxy position immediately. The safest route is past the wave on the river side: poison the wave behind his tower before it reaches him and back out before he can land Disdain (E) on you. At level 2 his Disdain (E) flip into Purge (W) is a kill combo if he lands it, so keep moving erratically and never stand still long enough for him to lock on a Q first.

notes: Killed a false claim repeated in three fields: Corrosive Charge does not deal percent-max-HP. Riot's text is 'dealing physical damage and slowing enemies caught in the explosion' — the page was telling a Singed his tankiness 'means nothing right now' on the strength of it. I did NOT touch the same claim where it is made about Purge (W): Riot's Data Dragon text for Purge says nothing about damage type at all, so the file cannot settle it either way and I left those sentences alone — see unverified. Added the two Disdain facts the entry never had: it shields him on the charge (the _missing rule for this pair), and it tramples non-champions, so a Singed hiding behind his own wave is not screened. Added Purge's self-slow as the exit cue, its 12/9/6/3/0 cooldown and zero cost at rank 5, and Fear Beyond Death's 2500 range. Level chart moved to the packet read (Urgot, Skill, Skill, Singed, Urgot, Singed, Urgot) — the old chart gave Singed four of seven stages in a 45.87% lane. NOT ASSERTED: Mega Adhesive grounds, and Riot describes Disdain as 'charges in a direction'. If grounding denies Disdain that is the single biggest fact in this matchup, but the kit carries no dash flag on Disdain and _missing has no enemy-dash-deniable rule for the pair, so I would not write it on inference — see questionsForUser. The Q 'dash' flag in urgot.json is a tooltip-parsing misfire; Corrosive Charge is thrown, not a dash, and I wrote nothing from it.
